series.evidence: Same flow as 241 West by hourly profile (AM peak 8-9am; labels are swapped between the counters), but not joined because the level is ~2.2x higher with no overlap to calibrate.

series.name: Counter 360 West (PM-peak direction)
series.evidence: Same flow as 241 East by hourly profile (PM peak 5-6pm), not joined because of the unexplained ~2.2x level change and no overlap.

useful: raw: ADDED_UPDATED dates showed the 2021-22 zeros were bulk-loaded on the day counting started, and Status showed the outage days are flagged warning
zeros(counter=True): found every outage with exact edges
duplicates/channels: showed each two-channel record published twice ([a,a,b,b]) on the flagged days
hourly: showed the East/West labels are swapped between counters 241 and 360
weekly(wide)+compare: level of each counter and the neighbour context
weather/compare by day: explained the late-July 2025 dip as heavy rain
not_useful: compare with 258: that site has its own level step in Aug 2023 and long zero runs, so ratios were noisy
improve: duplicates: merge runs across directions and give one row per date range
overview: output is wide and long; a pivot per month with directions as columns would be easier to read
add: a per-day load-date/status summary tool (records, warnings, load dates per counter-day) to spot back-filled placeholder zeros quickly

summary: Site 552 (Miller St, Pyrmont) has Ecocounter 241 (Oct 2021-Aug 2025) and Metrocount 360 (Oct 2025 on). Counter 241's first 5.5 months are back-filled zeros before counting began, it had four warning-flagged outages, and 28 day-runs where both channel records were published twice (drop_duplicates). Counter 360 reads ~2.2x the level of 241 with swapped direction labels and no overlap, so each counter-direction is its own series.
